questions.stem: Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) prevents ARP poisoning by:

choices.D: Validating ARP packets against a DHCP snooping binding table and dropping mismatches

questions.explanation: DAI checks incoming ARP replies against trusted DHCP snooping bindings, dropping fraudulent replies that don't match.

questions.stem: DDoS attacks use multiple sources to:

choices.C: Inject malicious code into web applications
choices.D: Overwhelm a target making it impractical to block by source IP

questions.explanation: DDoS uses a botnet of many hosts simultaneously, making the attack extremely difficult to filter by source.

choices.C: Encrypted DNS queries to be decrypted
choices.D: Users of the poisoned resolver to be redirected to the attacker's IP

questions.explanation: DNSSEC adds cryptographic signatures to DNS records so resolvers can verify responses are authentic and unmodified.

questions.stem: A SYN flood exploits the TCP handshake by:

choices.A: Completing handshakes rapidly to exhaust CPU
choices.B: Sending many SYNs with spoofed source IPs, filling the server's half-open connection table
choices.C: Intercepting SYN-ACK packets to steal session tokens
choices.D: Replaying SYN packets to re-establish expired connections

questions.explanation: SYN flood sends unanswered SYN packets. The server allocates resources for half-open connections waiting for ACKs that never arrive.

questions.stem: IP spoofing forges which packet field?
questions.explanation: IP spoofing creates packets with a false source IP, enabling impersonation of trusted hosts or obscuring attack origin.

questions.stem: Replay attacks are best defeated by:

choices.A: Time-limited tokens with nonces that cannot be reused

questions.explanation: Timestamps (expiry) and nonces (one-time values) make captured tokens useless after a very brief window.

questions.stem: Network segmentation limits attack impact by:

choices.B: Detecting attackers as they cross segment boundaries
choices.D: Restricting lateral movement so a compromised host cannot directly reach other segments

questions.explanation: Segmentation forces attackers to traverse controlled boundaries (firewalls, ACLs) to reach other segments, slowing them and creating detection opportunities.
